name: Liverpool FC
desc: Premier League football club with a global fan base, owned by Fenway Sports Group.
markets: UK and worldwide fan base, with large followings in Asia, Africa and North America
talks: FSG was reported to be in talks to sell a roughly 30% minority stake to an Amit Bhatia-led, Mittal-backed consortium at about a USD 6B valuation, per unnamed sources.
status_detail: Aug 2026: a consortium including Jeff Bezos agreed to buy about 30% for GBP 1.65B, valuing the club at GBP 5.5B (about USD 7B at current rates).
rationale: Global sports brand with new deep-pocketed investors; cross-promotion with F1 audiences and FSG's own Cadillac F1 interest.

name: New York Yankees (Yankee Global Enterprises)
desc: Major League Baseball franchise and parent company owning the YES Network and stadium interests.
markets: United States, with merchandise and fan base across Latin America, Japan and Europe
talks: Bloomberg and Sportico reported in July that the Yankees were in talks with Apollo over a USD 2-3B financing deal; the NY Post later said Apollo would take a 16% stake valuing the parent at significantly more than USD 12B.
talks_outlet: Bloomberg / Sportico (via Bleacher Report, NY Post)
status_detail: Aug 2026: the Yankees announced a USD 2.6B financing agreement with Apollo, a mix of debt and equity; stake size and valuation not officially disclosed.
rationale: Iconic US sports brand with fresh capital; US F1 growth and New York audience make cross-marketing plausible.

name: Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B)
desc: South Indian vegetarian restaurant and sweets chain with about 160 outlets in India and 30 overseas.
markets: India, Singapore, United States, Australia, Malaysia and the United Kingdom
talks: Mint reported Bodhi Tree (James Murdoch and Uday Shankar) in talks for a significant minority or majority stake at a Rs 3,000-3,500 crore valuation, mixing primary and secondary shares.
status_detail: 12 Nov 2026: Bodhi Tree Systems agreed to invest USD 180M for a majority stake; valuation about USD 350M per an industry source; primary/secondary split not disclosed.
rationale: Media-savvy new owners plan global expansion and a listing; F1 is a weak fit beyond Indian diaspora marketing.

name: Las Vegas Raiders
desc: National Football League franchise based in Las Vegas, controlled by Mark Davis.
markets: United States, with NFL international games and a global fan base
talks: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar, that a group led by Silver Lake's Egon Durban would buy 25% of the Raiders at a USD 9.9B valuation.
status_detail: The sale was approved by NFL owners in May 2026; Durban is described as the Raiders' largest minority owner by Oct 2026.
rationale: Las Vegas franchise sharing a city with the Las Vegas Grand Prix; owners with deep tech and media ties.

name: Cleveland Browns
desc: National Football League franchise owned by the Haslam Sports Group.
markets: United States, mainly Ohio and the wider NFL audience
talks: Bloomberg reported the Browns were selling a stake to Arctos Partners at a valuation above USD 9B; CBS put the initial stake at 3%.
status_detail: NFL owners approved the 3% sale to Arctos at the spring 2026 owners meeting.
rationale: Owner group runs multiple sports assets; F1 tie-up would be marketing-led rather than brand-led.

name: Atlanta Falcons
desc: National Football League franchise controlled by Arthur Blank, owner of Mercedes-Benz Stadium operations.
markets: United States, Atlanta and the wider NFL audience
talks: CNBC's Mike Ozanian reported that Arctos agreed to buy 10% of the Falcons at a USD 10.6B valuation; no team statement.
status_detail: 20 Oct 2026: the team announced Arctos bought a 7.5% stake, with 2.5% more committed, after NFL owner approval; valuation not restated.
rationale: Blank's group owns Mercedes-Benz Stadium relationship and Atlanta United; premium hospitality ties suit F1 hosting.

name: New York Islanders
desc: National Hockey League franchise playing at UBS Arena on Long Island.
markets: United States, New York metropolitan area
talks: Sportico reported the Islanders agreed to sell roughly 15% of shares at a USD 3B valuation; the team declined comment and NHL approval is pending.
status_detail: No team or NHL announcement found; last seen reported Oct 2026 (Forbes analysis of USD 3B value).
rationale: Owner Jon Ledecky is UK-based; New York audience overlaps with F1's US push, but team budgets are modest.

name: TMRW Sports
desc: Sports-tech venture of Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy that runs the TGL indoor golf league.
markets: United States broadcast audience via ESPN, with global golf fans and expansion ambitions
talks: Front Office Sports reported TMRW Sports is finalizing a new funding round that would value it at more than USD 1B, about double its 2024 Series A value; Dynasty Equity expected to take part.
raised_so_far: Not found; Series A in 2024 at nearly USD 500M valuation, per Gulf News
status_detail: No closing announcement found; still described as nearing a USD 1B value in Nov 2026 coverage.
rationale: Tech-led sports entertainment brand with star founders; F1 shares its premium, global, tech-savvy audience.

name: Cleveland Cavaliers
desc: National Basketball Association franchise controlled by Dan Gilbert, playing at Rocket Arena.
markets: United States, mainly Ohio and national NBA audiences
talks: MT Newswires reported Blue Owl Capital in advanced talks to buy a 5%-10% minority stake in the Cavaliers; valuation not given in the visible report.
status_detail: No deal announcement found; Cleveland.com said in late Jun 2026 Gilbert was moving closer to a minority sale.
rationale: Gilbert's Rocket companies are big sports sponsors; the team itself is a weak but affordable F1 tie-in.

name: Orbicular Pharmaceutical Technologies
desc: Develops complex generic and specialty drugs, including liraglutide and semaglutide peptides, licensed to global partners.
markets: Regulated and emerging drug markets, including the United States and Canada, through licensing partners
talks: Mint reported Warburg Pincus and CVC eyeing a stake in Orbicular in a deal valuing it at USD 1-1.5B; Jefferies advising, existing backer Tata Capital Healthcare Fund may exit.
status_detail: Formal sale process was expected to launch in the following quarter; no deal announcement found as of Nov 2026.
rationale: GLP-1 peptide maker gaining global scale; F1 would be corporate B2B hospitality rather than consumer branding.

name: Parfums de Marly
desc: French luxury niche fragrance house founded in 2009, owned by Advent International since 2023.
markets: Luxury department stores and perfumeries in Europe, the Middle East, the United States and Asia
talks: Reuters reported, citing two people familiar, that Advent is exploring a sale with CVC, Cinven and Puig among suitors; one source put the value below EUR 2B.
status_detail: Discussions ongoing as of 28 Oct 2026; no deal announced. EUR 2B converted at about 1.1 USD/EUR (approximate).
rationale: Luxury fragrance brand selling heavily in the Gulf and US; rivals in luxury already use F1 for prestige marketing.

name: Arthea (formerly PDC Brands)
desc: Personal care platform owning bath and body brands such as Dr Teal's, backed by CVC.
markets: US mass retail and drugstores, with some international distribution
talks: Reuters reported, citing sources, that owner CVC is exploring a sale of Arthea that could value it at around USD 2B; talks at an early stage.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Sep 2026.
rationale: Mass-market US personal care brands; F1's growing US female audience is a possible but weak fit.

name: Crystal Palace FC
desc: Premier League football club based in south London, led by chairman Steve Parish.
markets: UK, with Premier League broadcast audiences worldwide and European competition
talks: City AM reported, citing multiple sources, that Palace's owners value the club at GBP 900M and hired Raine Group to field interest in investment or a possible sale.
status_detail: No investment or sale announced as of Nov 2026. GBP 900M converted at about 1.33 USD/GBP (approximate).
rationale: London club seeking new capital; new owners may want global brand-building platforms, though budgets are tight.

name: Everton FC
desc: Premier League football club owned by The Friedkin Group, playing at the new Hill Dickinson Stadium.
markets: UK, with Premier League broadcast audiences worldwide
talks: The FT reported Everton's owners were looking for investors; Sky Sports later said The Friedkin Group hopes for upwards of GBP 1B in a sale.
talks_outlet: Financial Times / Sky Sports (via Goodison News)
status_detail: On 9 Oct 2026 the club confirmed TFG is exploring investment options and a potential sale; the GBP 1B price is unconfirmed and analysts value it nearer GBP 500M.
rationale: Owner Dan Friedkin also owns Toyota distribution and AS Roma; club itself is a weak F1 sponsor candidate.

name: LaserAway
desc: US chain of medical aesthetics clinics offering laser hair removal, injectables and skin treatments.
markets: United States, clinics across many states
talks: Reuters reported, citing people familiar, that Ares-backed LaserAway is exploring a sale that could value the medical spa chain at more than USD 2B.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Jun 2026.
rationale: Consumer aesthetics brand with heavy marketing spend; F1's growing US female audience could suit it.

name: True Religion
desc: US denim and casual apparel brand with about 60 stores and roughly USD 550M annual revenue.
markets: United States stores and wholesale, plus international licensing and e-commerce
talks: Reuters reported, citing sources, that ACON-owned True Religion is exploring options including a full or minority stake sale valuing it at close to USD 1B, with JPMorgan advising.
status_detail: Early-stage process as of 19 Oct 2026; no buyer identified.
rationale: Lifestyle fashion brand pushing store growth; F1's fashion crossover (Tommy, Puma) shows apparel fits.

name: Javvy
desc: Functional beverage brand known for protein coffee powders and concentrates sold online and at Walmart.
markets: United States e-commerce and mass retail, including Walmart nationwide
talks: Reuters reported, citing sources, that Javvy is exploring a sale that could value it at around USD 1B as demand for protein products grows.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Aug 2026.
rationale: Fast-growing energy and protein drink brand; energy drink rivals like Red Bull and Monster dominate F1.

name: Dose
desc: Maker of daily liquid wellness shots with elderberry, turmeric and ginger, with over USD 200M revenue.
markets: United States grocery, drugstore and online retail channels
talks: Reuters reported, citing people familiar, that Dose is exploring a sale with Perella Weinberg that could value it at close to USD 1B; investors include Unilever Ventures.
raised_so_far: Not found (investors Unilever Ventures, Melitas, Vanterra)
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Aug 2026. 'Close to USD 1B' may fall just short.
rationale: Wellness drink brand with strong margins; health-positioned beverages increasingly use sport sponsorship.

name: Brunt Workwear
desc: Direct-to-consumer brand selling work boots and workwear apparel to tradespeople.
markets: United States, online and through retail partners
talks: Reuters reported, citing sources, that Brunt Workwear is exploring a full sale or strategic investment that could value the private company at over USD 1B.
status_detail: No deal announcement found; last seen reported May 2026.
rationale: Brand built on blue-collar marketing; F1 is a stretch, but NASCAR-style trade audiences overlap with US F1 growth.

name: Rawlings Sporting Goods
desc: Baseball equipment and sporting goods maker co-owned by Seidler Equity Partners and Major League Baseball.
markets: United States, Japan, Latin America and other baseball markets
talks: Bloomberg reported Seidler Equity is exploring a sale of its 75% stake in Rawlings, seeking a valuation of about USD 2B including debt; Octus later said Partners Group was among interested sponsors.
status_detail: Auction underway with Jefferies advising as of Nov 2026; no deal announced.
rationale: Sporting goods brand; new owners may seek global marketing beyond baseball, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Custom Ink
desc: Online platform where customers design custom T-shirts, apparel and promotional merchandise for groups.
markets: United States consumers, schools, teams and businesses
talks: Reuters reported, citing people familiar, that Custom Ink is exploring a sale that could value it at close to USD 1.5B.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Oct 2026.
rationale: Merchandise platform; sports merchandising angle but limited brand-led need for F1.

name: Discovery Senior Living
desc: One of the largest US operators of senior housing and assisted living communities.
markets: United States, communities across many states
talks: Reuters reported, citing people familiar, that the owners of Discovery Senior Living are exploring a sale that could value it at more than USD 1B.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Oct 2026.
rationale: Domestic care operator; F1 sponsorship fit is very weak, listed only because it crosses the valuation line.

name: SuKarne
desc: Mexico's largest meat exporter, producing and distributing beef and other protein products.
markets: Mexico, United States, Japan, South Korea and other export markets
talks: Reuters reported, citing people familiar, that SuKarne's owner is exploring a sale that could value the company at over USD 2B.
status_detail: No sale announcement found; last seen reported Aug 2026.
rationale: Large Mexican exporter; Mexico City Grand Prix offers a home-market hospitality platform.

name: Iconix International
desc: Brand management company owning and licensing fashion and sports brands such as Umbro and Starter.
markets: Licensing partners across North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America
talks: WWD reported, citing sources, that Iconix hired J.P. Morgan to find a buyer in a sale that could be worth about USD 1B.
status_detail: Modaes reported talks with several prospective buyers in Oct 2026; no deal announced.
rationale: Owns Umbro and other sports-heritage labels; licensing model could use F1 for brand visibility.

name: Cloudnine Hospitals (Kids Clinic India)
desc: Chain of maternity, fertility and paediatric hospitals operating across major Indian cities.
markets: India, hospitals in Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai and other cities
talks: Reports said TPG and Permira were frontrunners to buy a roughly 25% stake from True North at a valuation of about Rs 11,000 crore.
talks_outlet: The Economic Times (via Digital Health News)
raised_so_far: True North invested about Rs 400 crore in 2015, per Outlook Business
status_detail: Permira filed to buy 25.71% of Kids Clinic India at about Rs 11,000 crore; CCI approved on 13 Oct 2026. Rupees converted at about 88.5 per USD (approximate).
rationale: Consumer-facing healthcare brand with new PE owner; F1 fit limited to Indian premium audiences.

name: AIG Hospitals
desc: Hyderabad-based multispecialty hospital group best known for gastroenterology and liver care services.
markets: India, mainly Hyderabad and Telangana, with medical tourism patients
talks: The Economic Times reported Novo Holdings, GIC and Axight in talks to invest Rs 2,000-2,500 crore in AIG Hospitals as founders pare 10-12% at a Rs 24,000 crore valuation.
status_detail: No deal announcement found; reported 14 Oct 2026. Rupees converted at about 88.5 per USD (approximate).
rationale: Large private hospital group with medical tourism ambitions; F1 fit is weak beyond corporate hospitality.
